I purchased this game as part of the Saints Row Ultimate Franchise Pack, which was on sale at the time for about $18.  I can honestly say this game has left me completely satisfied with my purchase, and despite having bought the bundle at the beginning of the summer, and played every day, it was at least a month before I even opened Saints Row 3 for the first time, because I was having so much fun playing Saints Row 2, and there is simply that much to do.  With 233.8 hours on record as of my review, I still am only at about 95-97% completion on my first and only playthrough, because it was simply too much fun screwing around.  Even after finishing the story missions, of which there are more than enough to make the game worth buying all by itself, there was still so much to do. 

 The controls took a bit of getting used to, but only at first.  After a short while, any oddities control-wise felt completely natural, which is far from always the case when talking about ported titles.  The only thing I could recommend a controller for would be the driving/piloting.  While driving ground vehicles, the WASD keys don't quite give you the best experience, but they work perfectly fine for it.  The main complaint I had about the game in general were the flight controls, which were awkward at first, but even after getting used to the layout, which wasn't that strange, it still lacked the ability to make small adjustments without losing control, unless you practice a lot. (I practiced a lot though, and mostly was able to work around it.) I got so accustomed to the keybindings in this game that I actually changed most of my SR3 keybindings to match (where they were different at least) because I found I honestly missed many of the default keybindings where they had been changed.  Still, using a console controller for the air vehicles is probably your best option, if nothing else.  

The graphics are far from amazing by current standards, but considering the time the game was made, they're perfectly solid, and the water still looks more real than watch dogs (you actually have a wake in a boat! HOW ADVANCED!! Sorry had to. considering I got this game in a huge bundle for only 18 dollars, I am not only satisfied, I would gladly have paid $18 dollars for this game alone, if I evaluated the value of the game solely on the amount of fun I had playing it.  All in all, I fully recommend this game and hope others enjoy it as much as I have.

[h1] Story [/h1]
As with every Saints Row game, it's not hard to predict the progression of our story, which is pretty standard. Basically, what you do is eliminate everyone in high positions one by one until you become the owner of the city, and along the way, you take out the lower-level guys and mid-level thugs, etc. :D Only a couple of parts of the game's story surprised me, upset me, or made me happy. : D If we skip over the writing of the story, the execution seems good. For example, in a boss battle where you expect to win, the ending can be different, and what the main character does in the credits at the end satisfies you. So, we have a simple, standard but well-executed story :)  The side quests are so fun and varied that the game doesn't bore you. If you want to do a little bit of each side quest alongside the main story to have a good gaming experience, then this game is perfect for you. But if you're thinking, “I'm going to do everything and finish all the side quests,” then it might get boring because the final levels of the side quests are quite challenging :) So, I wouldn't push too hard to complete everything 100%. Instead, I'd recommend enjoying each side quest at a 2-3 level pace, relaxing and having fun alongside the main story quests :)


[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
We present one of the classic GTA-style games :D Our game features the classic gameplay of an action-based third-person shooter open world game. However, what sets it apart from the GTA series is its fluid and fun gameplay. In fact, what sets our game apart from similar titles in terms of gameplay, story, and many other aspects is its fun structure. In terms of playtime, it's possible to finish our game in about 30-35 hours total, of course, if you don't grind for 100% completion :D So, for those who want a long playtime, the game offers us a medium-to-long playtime; it's neither too short nor too long and boring :)


[h1] Graphics [/h1]
The graphics are generally quite adequate, the drawings aren't bad; the only problem is the irregularity of the textures, like passing through walls :D Or not being able to knock over huge lamps and trees :D These are inevitable in old games, especially old open world games, but they could have been solved with a couple of updates if someone had bothered. Also, considering the year it was released, the car models and modifications are quite satisfying. I'd say it's a good game even now, and I think it can still hold its own against many new games :D Especially finding lots of cool cars, modifying them, and putting them in my driveway has always been a source of joy for me in open-world games like GTA. Driving them, taking their photos, or simply keeping them in the garage because I love them too much to part with them :D As someone who loves these things, the game's car design and modification features have personally satisfied me.


[h1] Final Thoughts [/h1]
Overall, our game is quite enjoyable. If you don't necessarily need an experience like GTA 5, which is among the best open-world games today, and you're not just someone who's obsessed with playing GTA 5, this is a very nice open-world game that can satisfy you quite well. It has a structure that GTA San Andreas fans will easily love :D Considering past standards, it's a game that stands out between GTA and Sleeping Dogs, especially with its enjoyable gameplay that breaks away from the seriousness between the two, and is occasionally hilarious :D If it goes on sale, don't miss it—it's a game that more than deserves its sale price. But whether it's worth buying at its regular price is up for debate ;)

For my 100th review, I had to review a very special game. Saints Row 2 is one of my favorite games of all time, and I have played a lot of games.

Before I talk about the game itself, keep in mind that this is one of the worst PC ports you can come across. But don’t worry, there is a community made mod called Juiced Patch that fixes almost everything. It makes the game play the way it should on PC and adds several quality of life features, such as uncapped FPS, faster loading times, removing the orange filter, and much more.

The community also restored the console exclusive DLC, and it is fully playable on PC.

I highly recommend installing Juiced Patch + the DLC. If you have modded games before, you already know what to do. If you’re new to modding, don’t worry, it’s very easy. Just download the files and drag them into the game folder. Follow any YouTube guide, and it should only take about five minutes. The patch also brings back the co-op mode.

Thanks to the patch, I was finally able to 100% the game, including all of the collectibles, without a single bug or crash. It feels great to be able to revisit one of my favorite games on PC whenever I want.

That said, I truly believe Saints Row 2 is the best crime game ever made.

Stilwater is an amazing city. Looking at the map, you might think it’s just an average sized open world, but it isn’t. The city feels alive and is packed with interior locations that you can explore, many of which are not even marked on the map. It’s an incredibly fun world to mess around in, especially in co-op, where you and a friend can create endless chaos.

The story is also excellent. It has the perfect balance between serious moments and over the top fun, which is what made Saints Row so unique. Sadly, Saints Row: The Third leaned too heavily into the goofy side, and the series gradually lost some of that original balance. And let’s not even talk about the reboot.

A lot of people label Saints Row 1 and 2 as GTA clones, but that comparison is often oversimplified. They share a genre, but Saints Row have its own identity rather than just copying GTA.

I also don’t think it makes sense to dismiss games just because they compete in the same space. Having multiple strong games in a genre is a good thing, it pushes all of them to improve. You can enjoy both GTA and Saints Row without needing to pick a side.

More competition = better games.

If you want to play a classic crime game, give Saints Row 2 a chance and see for yourself why so many people still love it. And if you’re already a fan and want to experience it again on PC, Juiced Patch has you covered.

Even with a bad pc port that might never receive the official patch it deserves, Saints Row 2 is still an amazing game and is worth playing if you consider yourself a fan of crime open world games.

I’m glad I decided to play this game! The only reason I started playing it was because I finished Saints Row 4 and loved it, which made me want more. As it turns out Saints Row 2 feels like it hardly belongs in the same franchise as the fourth game. Volition have truly reinvented the franchise as they’ve gone from title to title, only keeping the characters and setting as they go. This explains why the people who loved the second game and wanted more of that tend to complain loudly about the third and fourth games. They’re just not the same. Personally I think reinventing and iterating are both equally valid approaches for a series to take. I like the variety, and you certainly can’t accuse them of retreading the same ground like I’ve seen some do with Rockstar and the GTA series.

Saints Row 2 came out in 2008, and it feels like a game of its time. It might not seem like 2008 is that far back, but when you play games of that time they all feel old now, as does Saints Row 2. At that time I remember games journalists were talking about emergent gameplay instead of story, and it shows in Saints Row 2’s design. Compared to any major game released in 2013 this feels like complete chaos. Instead of the world acting like a virtual movie set with carefully staged combat, the game instead relies on world simulation systems and AI to act on its own. This approach makes it nearly impossible for a developer to tell a story during missions, because the minute to minute gameplay is completely unpredictable. Instead the designer only choreographs the action with commands like: Go there, kill that, chase that car, etc. 

Even during missions the world simulation present in the free exploration mode is in full effect. So when you take over areas of the map you’ll have friendly thugs spawn there. If a mission happens to take place there, or a car chase goes through neighborhoods controlled by your gang, groups of friendly thugs will spawn and rain bullets on your pursuers. If during a mission an enemy shoots a civilian standing near you, police will arrive on the scene and start fighting the enemy gangsters with you. The last time I saw this kind of three way combat break out spontaneously was in the Stalker games. I wish we had more games like this, especially on the next-gen consoles where the extra memory and power could allow much more elaborate world simulation. That would in some way fulfill “the point” of next-gen hardware. Making something you couldn’t do on 360/ps3, just like this game is something that couldn’t exist on PS2.

Anyway, I had a great time blowing through this game. It’s messy, ugly, glitch, but it all comes together to create something special. One thing I was pleasantly surprised by was the quality of the cutscenes. In Saints Row 4 they were generally very high quality, but in a couple scenes I found the sound to be a bit crap. In Saints Row 2 the sound during cutscenes is phenomenal. It’s raw, violent and has about as much impact as you could hope to have. It fits perfectly with the story itself which in the “Brotherhood” missions turns into an ugly conflict where neither side appear noble or heroic in any way. It’s dark, gruesome and I was even shocked at one scene where the game made it abundantly clear that the player isn’t a hero anyone should aspire to be. So I finally get where the hype about Saints Row 2 has come from. If you know you’re a fan of slightly janky games with outstanding qualities you’ll probably like this. Those wanting a slick, modern, controlled experience should avoid it like the plague.

After waking up from a coma caused by a traumatic blast from a bombing, a notorious gangster breaks out of prison and seeks to reclaim the city they once handed to their old gang. But with that gang mostly disbanded, it's time for our protagonist to take reforming the gang on their own shoulders alongside an old friend and take the fight to the new players in town.

Saints Row 2 is a sequel to the great but widely unavailable original Saints Row, elevating the first game in many ways aside from now being widely available on more than one platform. It follows in Saints Row's footsteps by maintaining the predacessor's grounded nature and street gangster roots where the games that follow after took much... Wilder and (in my opinion) weaker directions.

Set five years after the events of Saints Row, we join the player character waking up from a coma in Stilwater's prison where we're introduced near immediately to character customisation. In some departures from the original, where the player character was a male silent protagonist, SR2 gives us six voices to choose from and the choice of playing as a female. All six voice actors for the protagonist do a good job of capturing the feel of the setting and how the character should be. And the player character... Can be absolutely psychotic. The sheer brutality on display with how the protagonist eliminates those close to the leader of the gangs (or the leader themselves) is eye opening when you hold them up to how the main character acts in Saints Row 3 and 4 where they become a shadow of their former selves as the franchise got sillier when trying to not act as a GTA clone.

Joining us in the escape from prison is Carlos, a fellow inmate who later becomes a member of the Saints who also does a little expositing as to what's changed in Stilwater since the events of the first game. Some of the original Saints went straight, the leader's vanished and one of your closest friends is now chief of police. Not only that, but three new gangs are controlling parts of Stilwater. The Ronin, who control their territory through vices like gambling and prositution. The Sons of Samedi, who control the flow of drugs that keep the students of Stilwater University happy with their their patented Loa Dust. And The Brotherhood, who don't really have deep rooted rackets like the other two but instead enforce themselves through intimdation and violence to take what they want.

But to even take on these gangs, you're gonna need some help. Aside from Carlos, players will reunite with Johnny Gat and meet some new people to head up with gathering intel and figuring out the best ways to make these gangs hurt. However, taking on these gangs is going to require an ounce of Respect. Doing actions and stunts to earn Respect will give access to story missions. Respect is also earned through the various activities the player can do not only for the Respect and monetary gain, but at levels 3 and 6 of a particular activity, you'll gain rewards. From store discounts, new weapons, health and stamina upgrades to infinite weapon ammo for a particular type.

Progressing through the story will even unlock things tied to the gang that you're taking on. From unarmed fighting styles, taunts and gestures, to the entire roster of vehicles that a particular gang uses with their decals.

Stilwater remains the same in terms of map layout from the original Saints Row. Taking back territory is as simple as completing story missions against each of the gangs and taking on their Strongholds, tough but short assaults against a notable location within Stilwater to wrestle control for your gang to move freely around it and provide a source of income for you to get at safehouses dotted around the map. That money can be put to use in buying up various businesses within your controlled territory for further income boosts, vehicles from dealerships if you can't find a particular vehicle you want for your collection, clothes that you have a good deal of choice when it comes to appearance and weapons to give yourself some slightly better firepower against your enemies.

For those who've played the later titles, don't expect the same mechanics when it comes to gameplay. With a camera that's centered on the character, a near lack of recoil when it comes to firing weapons, it almost feels closer to the 3D trilogy of GTA games. There's also no leveling up or skills to buy with cash or Respect, no weapon upgrades from gun stores and (a way more obvious thing to point out) nothing zany or gimmicky when it comes to weapons. As I said before, this is a much more street level and grounded game when compared to what comes after. The Reboot tries to balance the street level stuff with some ridiculous quirks in gameplay, but I just cling to SR2's gameplay more than the games that followed.

My only real criticism with SR2 (aside from it being a HORRIBLE PC port), is the difficulty of certain activities when you get to the higher tiers. Like the much infamous Tow Truck diversion which I just cheesed by getting gang members off the streets to jump into the cars I needed to tow and follow me to the drop off point. This avoided ALL of the pursuers one would get when picking up one of the cars and having to drive it all the way to the drop off point while under constant attack. Not to mention how awful driving is when towing a vehicle.

Otherwise, Saints Row 2 is easily the best of the series. Having played all but the original I feel like it's easy for me to put it on such a pedestal. I highly recommend picking up Saints Row 2 and experiencing it for yourself. If you follow my note at the top of this review and install the Juiced Patch, I guarantee you'll have a great time with this game.

Saints Row 2... oh boy. This game is something special, both in a good and bad way. In a good way, it's Saints Row 2; a fairly huge open world crime sandbox that lets you be almost any character your mind can imagine. On top of this you can drive almost any vehicle you wish and run around the city getting into some of the most crazy and action packed shenanigans any game could ever offer.

What made me put a thumbs down though? It's an absolute crapfest of a PC port. I didn't do my research, so I wasn't aware that the PC port was bad until after I purchased it. Thank the Saints I got it on sale. Even with the right mods that allegedly "fix" the game, it is still a hassle to get working for more than an hour. Nearly every corner of this port is infested with the mediocrity. The audio is plagued with issues, the vehicle controls are either too clunky or too jerky, (the gunplay is alright), the game's framerate will tank after about an hour of gameplay, and perhaps the worst part; it crashes. Alot. One of the easiest ways to crash it is to go into an outfit or clothing menu. This is hell on earth for me, as I constantly want to change my character's outfit whenever I play a game like this.

My sypnosis? It's still an OK game, but I would not get it on PC unless it is on sale. I still managed to beat the game, but the bugs left me tired of the game, and wanting to beat it as quickly as possible.

My thoughts: Everyone should leave a negative review on this game in protest. 
The Steam version is shipped with broken content, filled with crashes, major FPS drops regardless of your hardware, and other really odd bugs.

Using a patch (either Gentlemen of the Row or Juiced) you can fix this, but it's even still not recommended to use the steam executable, which is broken. I had to buy the game on GoG (luckily it's on sale right now), grab the executable from there, replace the steam executable, install a patch, and now the game seems to work smoothly with more FPS.

The sad thing is, this is not the only game on steam that ships in a broken state. There's several others, generally really crappy PC ports or really old games, that require patches before they'll even boot. I can't in good faith stand by these practices, so instead of reviewing the actual game (which I really enjoy), I'll leave my negative review for visibility.

Hello Friends. This is the original saints row game on steam that i have played. I actually never played the original one, so this is the first one i played. This is the game that introduces you to many of the saints row characters that you have come and known. I haven't played the game recently, but i have played it in the past. It seems many people are complaining it does not work very good on windows 10. I myself have not tested it myself, but it might have to do with the same thing i did for Saints row 4, by limiting how many processors run for the game. This game is more like a GTA game than the others in the series. I actually did not like it as much as the later ones that are more silly and funny. I want to laugh and forget my worries of the day so i like funny and silly games like the later ones. Still, if you want to play a game that is similiar to GTA, play this one. Otherwise, you can buy this game to find out what the saints are referencing in the later games in the series.

Recommended for being a saints row game, even thought it is more GTA style like playing.

This game has to be one of my favorites of all time. 
Character creation is amazing, so many customization options. I made Nigel Thornberry.
The story is actually really good and immersive and invokes genuine feelings, you really hate the antagonists. 
The game is just the right amount of crazy, the third and fourth games went off the deep end and while they were still entertaining, the story wasn't really as serious as it was in this game.
The difficulty was alright, it wasn't irrationally hard but it didn't seem overly easy.
It was genuinely fun to play and the characters were well developed.
I highly recommend the game, it's definitely worth the money and time. My only negative thing is the multiplayer, it's very difficult to connect with friends, but possible. I do truly love this game despite that, and it's definitely worth the dollars.
